anya: Heads-up: onboarding hydra-v2-lite embeddings. After ONNX int6-pertensor conversion I'm seeing a noticeable spike in centroid displacement across weekly slices for newswire-weekly-12m. Recall@10 dropped ~1.9% compared to fp16 baseline on the latest week. Anyone seen this pattern when quantizing?

sam: what's the split and eval command?

anya: split=wk10..wk31. Command used:

```
python run_eval.py \
  --model hydra-v2-lite \
  --quant onnx-int6 \
  --calib none \
  --dataset newswire-weekly-12m \
  --split weekly \
  --metrics recall@1,5,10,centroid_shift,silhouette
```

Quick aggregated numbers:
- fp16: @1=0.488, @5=0.691, @10=0.761, silhouette=0.195, centroid_shift_avg=0.0098
- int6-pertensor: @1=0.481, @5=0.678, @10=0.742, silhouette=0.171, centroid_shift_avg=0.0156

ravi: centroid_shift nearly 60% higher on int6. Did you apply global mean subtract + L2 norm?

anya: global mean from preproc, then L2. No per-slice centering.

toni: try per-channel calibration and also a tiny rescaling (learned scalar) on embeddings before indexing. Sometimes quant compresses dynamic range.

mlbot: eval-bot: queued job 9021 for hydra-v2-lite int6-perchannel calibration (user=anya).

anya: queued. Also tested checkpoint ensemble behaviour (mean of checkpoints vs quant avg):
- fp16-mean(ckpt{0,3,6}) @10 = 0.773
- quant(mean->quant) @10 = 0.754
- quant->mean @10 = 0.763
So averaging before quantizing wins over quantize-then-avg.

sam: that suggests quantization noise has non-zero mean across model snapshots. Ensemble ordering should be part of onboarding notes.

anya: spun a PCA on weekly centroids. First principal component captures ~52% variance and the int6 bias projects strongly onto PC1. If we remove ~0.02 projection along PC1 from int6 embeddings, centroid_shift drops ~0.004 but recall only improves ~0.002.

ravi: worth automating as optional debias step for indexing if it consistently helps. Also try increasing HNSW ef_search from 64->200 during experiments; search robustness can hide small embedding perturbations.

toni: add to checklist: 1) int6 per-channel calibration using stratified weekly sample (10k per week), 2) ensemble averaging before quantization when using multi-ckpt, 3) try ef_construction=200, ef_search=200 for int6 indexes, 4) run temperature scaling on similarity logits.

anya: infra note: ran on staging-gpu-b (cuda 12.1, onnxrt 1.16) with ONNX flag `ORT_USE_IO_THREADPOOL=1`. infra-bot: confirm parity with prod?

infra-bot: prod uses onnxrt 1.16 and same env flags; staging-gpu-b matches.

mlbot: job 9021 completed: artifacts -> s3://redwood-evals/hydra/v2/onboard/1743220000/job-9021/

anya: interim results from int6-perchannel calibration:
- int6-perchannel @10 = 0.755 (was 0.742), centroid_shift_avg=0.0112, silhouette=0.181
- reindexed with ef_construction=200 + ef_search=200: int6 @10 = 0.761

sam: nice improvement. If per-channel + index tuning brings us within ~0.01 of fp16, we can recommend int6 for non-SLA tiers.

ravi: if after 3-week rolling check it's still stable, let's add a callout to onboard docs with sample calibration script and PCA debias snippet. I can help PR the scripts.

toni: one more test: try int8-perchannel quick run to compare. If int8 gets closer to fp16 with similar cost, may be preferred.

anya: scheduling int8 run now. Will post results tomorrow AM. Attaching artifacts + plots to model onboarding ticket when complete.

anya: thanks all, appreciate the quick eyes.
